hypothesis: ARC-R036 showed that all 216 deeper execution failures arise because separator structure is destroyed and lattice topology is then re-inferred from the mutated grid. Carrying the original separator-defined partition topology across steps will remove that closure blocker and may make an exact depth-4 program reachable.
baseline: ARC-R035 shared-overlap alignment search, diagnosed by ARC-R036
primary_change: Infer separator-defined variable-span region topology once from each original input and keep that topology immutable across subsequent lattice_peer_reduce steps instead of re-inferring partitions from mutated grid pixels.
split: permitted public ARC-AGI-2 training data only
frozen_controls: ARC-R034 variable-span separator inference semantics at initial partition construction
primary_metric: exact training-consistent program under bounded deterministic search
success_threshold: Eliminate the separator_structure_lost blocker and find at least one exact training-consistent program within depth 4.
partial_success: separator_structure_lost failures are eliminated or materially reduced and deeper transitions expand, but no exact program is found.
falsification: If persistent initial topology does not remove the dominant separator-loss failure class, or removes it without improving bounded reachability/near-miss structure, reject topology persistence as the sufficient next semantic mechanism.
adversarial_interpretation: ARC-R036 proves a transition-closure blocker, not solution sufficiency. Identity was already the closest reachable state by cell-error distance, so even perfect topology persistence may leave the operator family semantically wrong.
